categories.main_business_segments: D.R. Horton operates through five main business segments: homebuilding (its core business), rental (single-family and multi-family rental operations), Forestar (a majority-owned residential lot development company), financial services (mortgage financing and title agency services), and other activities (including insurance-related operations, water rights, and non-residential real estate). Homebuilding generates the vast majority of revenue, with rental, Forestar, and financial services providing diversification and vertical integration.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company primarily utilizes a decentralized operating model for homebuilding, relying on local management teams for site selection, land acquisition, and construction management. Construction and land development are performed almost entirely by subcontractors, selected through competitive bidding. D.R. Horton leverages economies of scale for procurement, employs standardized home designs with local customization, and uses technology systems for operational oversight, risk management, and customer engagement.
categories.primary_customers_markets: D.R. Horton serves a broad range of homebuyers, with a primary focus on entry-level and first-time move-up buyers, but also offers homes for active adult and luxury segments. Its customers include individual homebuyers, institutional investors (for rental properties), and other homebuilders (through Forestar lot sales). The company’s end markets are primarily residential housing (for sale and rental), with some exposure to land development and mortgage/title services.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in 126 markets across 36 states, organized into six reporting regions: Northwest, Southwest, South Central, Southeast, East, and North. Major states include Texas, Florida, California, North Carolina, and Georgia, with significant presence in both high-growth Sunbelt and established Midwest/Northeast markets. Forestar, the lot development subsidiary, operates in 64 markets across 23 states, often overlapping with D.R. Horton’s homebuilding footprint.
categories.supply_chain_position: D.R. Horton is primarily a downstream operator, acting as a homebuilder and seller to end customers, but also integrates midstream activities through its majority ownership of Forestar (land development) and its rental and financial services segments. The company controls a significant portion of its land and lot supply through contracts and its relationship with Forestar, enhancing supply chain control and efficiency.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, D.R. Horton focuses on geographic and product diversification, operational efficiency, and risk management. Key priorities include maintaining a flexible lot supply, controlling costs, leveraging digital marketing, and investing in rental operations to capture demand in high-growth markets. The company emphasizes continuous improvement, talent development, and sustainability initiatives, including energy efficiency, responsible land development, and water management. R&D is not a primary focus, but innovation is pursued in construction methods, digital engagement, and customer experience.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale of completed homes (92% of consolidated revenues), with additional income from land and lot sales (via Forestar), rental property sales, mortgage origination and sales, and title services. Rental income is recognized as other income, while mortgage loans are typically sold to third-party purchasers shortly after origination. The company also earns ancillary income from insurance, water rights, and non-residential real estate.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States by volume and has held this position since 2002. Key competitors include other national homebuilders such as Lennar, PulteGroup, and KB Home, as well as regional and local builders. The company competes on price, location, product quality, and financing terms, and is also a major player in the fragmented lot development industry through Forestar. Its scale, geographic reach, and vertical integration provide competitive advantages.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2025, D.R. Horton reported consolidated revenues of $34.3 billion, pre-tax income of $4.7 billion, and net income of $3.6 billion. The company closed 84,863 homes with an average price of $370,400. While revenues and home closings declined 7% and 5% year-over-year, respectively, D.R. Horton remains highly profitable with strong cash flows and a robust balance sheet. The company maintains significant liquidity and a moderate leverage profile, with a long-term focus on sustainable growth and market share consolidation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: D.R. Horton emphasizes affordability, geographic and product diversity, and operational efficiency as its core value propositions. Its scale enables cost advantages, broad product offerings, and flexibility to adjust to local market conditions. The company’s decentralized model empowers local teams to tailor homes to buyer preferences, while its integrated financial and title services streamline the customer experience. D.R. Horton’s reputation for quality, reliability, and customer service, along with its strong balance sheet, further differentiate it from competitors.
